format: storytime: the move after the win
title: The move after the W

verse.sanskrit:
मरणान्तानि वैराणि निर्वृत्तं नः प्रयोजनम् ।
क्रियतामस्य संस्कारो ममाप्येष यथा तव ॥
verse.iast:
maraṇāntāni vairāṇi nirvṛttaṃ naḥ prayojanam |
kriyatām asya saṃskāro mamāpy eṣa yathā tava ||
verse.translation: Enmity ends with death. Our purpose is done. Let his last rites be performed; he is as much mine as yours.

beats.title: the move AFTER the win
beats.vo: The war is over. Ravana has fallen. Rama just won the biggest W in the whole epic.

beats.title: now what?
beats.vo: Now's the moment for the victory lap. The trash talk. The posting on main.
Instead, Ravana's brother Vibhishana is grieving. He says: he was my brother, let me give him his last rites. And Rama says yes. Fully.
Enmity ends with death. Our purpose is done. Give him his rites. He is as much mine as yours.

beats.title: When it's over, let it be over
beats.vo: That's the real flex. Win the fight, then drop the beef.
The match is done, the argument's settled, the breakup is old news? Stop re-fighting it in your head. Rama didn't.

beats.title: Day 6 of learning from Rama
beats.vo: Day six of learning from Rama. Follow for day seven.

music_suggestions: A slow, emotional flute or shehnai track from Instagram's library
caption:
Rama's move after winning the war? Not a victory lap. 🤍

When Vibhishana grieved for his brother Ravana, Rama told him to give Ravana full last rites.

“मरणान्तानि वैराणि निर्वृत्तं नः प्रयोजनम् । क्रियतामस्य संस्कारो ममाप्येष यथा तव ॥”
Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda 112.26

When it's over, let it be over. Day 6 of learning from Rama.
